Run a DuckDB query and receive the result exactly

Source: R/duckdb.R
arrow_duckdb.Rd

arrow_duckdb() runs sql on a DuckDB connection and returns the result as a data frame. The rows travel as an Arrow stream, so every column is converted as arrow_to_r() converts it: exactly, or with an error that names the column.

Usage

arrow_duckdb(con, sql, to = NULL, lossy = zar_lossy_policies)

Arguments

con

A connection from DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb()).

sql

The query, a single string.

to

NULL, or a named list of prototypes, one per column. For an array that is not a struct, a single prototype.

lossy

What to do with a column R cannot hold exactly.

Value

A data frame.

Details

The query runs with DuckDB's arrow_lossless_conversion setting on. Then HUGEINT and UHUGEINT arrive as the arrow.opaque extension over fixed_size_binary(16), not as a decimal128(38, 0) that cannot be told from a real decimal. Without a registration for them, they pass through as a list of 16-byte raw vectors that keeps the extension in its attributes. The setting is put back as it was when the call returns.

A BIGINT whose values all lie within ±2^53 becomes a double. A value beyond that is a zuarrow_lossy_error naming 'zuint' under the default policy, as for any int64 column. A package that registers exact classes with arrow_register() makes such columns exact.

It needs the 'DBI', 'duckdb' (1.5.4 or later) and 'nanoarrow' packages.

See also

arrow_to_r() for the conversion and its policies.

Examples

con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpaHpEpc/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
arrow_duckdb(con, "SELECT 42::BIGINT AS id, 'a' AS label")
#>   id label
#> 1 42     a

big <- "SELECT 9007199254740993::BIGINT AS id"
try(arrow_duckdb(con, big))
#> Error in arrow_duckdb(con, big) : 
#>   Column `id` (Arrow format `l`) can't be converted to R exactly: row 1 holds 9007199254740993. Load zuint to read it exactly, or use `lossy = "character"` for its exact text, or `lossy = "allow"` to accept the loss.
arrow_duckdb(con, big, lossy = "character")
#>                 id
#> 1 9007199254740993
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
